title: Nickel: NiCd and NiMH

concepts.label: nickel oxyhydroxide electrode
concepts.definition: The positive electrode of all nickel cells: solid NiO(OH) takes one electron and one H from water to become solid Ni(OH)2 (Ni +3 to +2), NiO(OH) + H2O + e- <-> Ni(OH)2 + OH-, E° = +0.49 V in base, 289 mAh per gram of Ni(OH)2.

concepts.label: NiCd cell
concepts.definition: A rechargeable cell with a cadmium anode (Cd + 2OH- -> Cd(OH)2 + 2e-, -0.81 V) and a NiO(OH) cathode in KOH: Cd + 2NiO(OH) + 2H2O <-> Cd(OH)2 + 2Ni(OH)2, E° = 1.30 V, about 1.2 V in use.

concepts.label: electrolyte not consumed (KOH)
concepts.definition: In nickel cells the OH- used at the negative electrode is returned at the nickel electrode, so the KOH concentration stays almost constant; the electrolyte is a carrier, not a reactant, and cannot reveal the state of charge.

concepts.label: flat discharge curve
concepts.definition: A voltage that stays on a plateau (about 1.2 V for nickel cells) for most of the discharge and drops sharply only at the end, because solids convert into solids while the electrolyte stays unchanged; contrast the steadily sliding curve of an alkaline primary cell.

concepts.label: memory effect
concepts.definition: After many identical partial discharge/recharge cycles a NiCd cell delivers the unused part of its charge at a lower voltage (a step in the curve), which a device reads as lost capacity; a full discharge and charge largely restores it.

concepts.label: metal hydride (hydrogen storage alloy)
concepts.definition: An alloy such as LaNi5 that holds hydrogen atoms in the gaps between its metal atoms (up to LaNi5H6, 372 mAh/g); as an electrode in KOH it reacts MH + OH- <-> M + H2O + e- at about -0.83 V.

concepts.label: NiMH cell
concepts.definition: A rechargeable cell with a metal hydride anode and a NiO(OH) cathode in KOH: MH + NiO(OH) <-> M + Ni(OH)2, one H atom per electron moving between the two solids, E° = 1.32 V, about 1.2 V in use.

concepts.label: self-discharge
concepts.definition: The slow loss of stored charge in an unused cell through side reactions inside it (for example NiO(OH) oxidising OH- to O2), expressed in per cent per month, faster when warm and reversed by recharging.

concepts.label: cycle life
concepts.definition: The number of full charge-discharge cycles a rechargeable cell survives before its capacity has fallen to 80% of the original value.

concepts.label: nickel–iron (Edison) cell
concepts.definition: A NiO(OH) cathode with an iron anode (Fe + 2OH- -> Fe(OH)2 + 2e-, about -0.88 V): very long-lived and cheap, but iron lies above the H2O/H2 rung so charging also makes hydrogen gas.

concepts.label: nickel–hydrogen cell
concepts.definition: A NiO(OH) cathode with pressurised hydrogen gas as the anode reactant (H2 + 2NiO(OH) <-> 2Ni(OH)2), used in satellites for its tens of thousands of cycles.

namedOnly: internal voltage loss under load (used in the capstone model as ohms per ampere; taught in Real batteries as internal resistance)
voltage depression from overcharging (mentioned as the commoner look-alike of the memory effect)
low-self-discharge NiMH (2005; one curve in the self-discharge widget)
molar volume of a gas (about 24.8 L/mol at 25 °C and 1 bar, stated as a fact)
lanthanum and mixed rare-earth alloys (LaNi5 as the example alloy; La mass 138.9 g/mol given locally)
oxygen recombination in sealed cells (not covered)
water stability limit for very negative electrodes (pointer to the lithium lesson)
platinum-coated hydrogen electrode (catalyst is taught in Hydrogen and fuel cells)
summary: Running example: an AA cell that stores 2.0 Ah (0.0746 mol of electrons, about 6.9 g of Ni(OH)2 at 289 mAh/g), built first as NiCd and then as NiMH around the same NiO(OH)/Ni(OH)2 electrode (Ni +3 <-> +2, +0.49 V) in KOH. An animated sealed cell with tile electrodes and an OH-/water ledger shows that the electrolyte is only borrowed (contrast with lead-acid), which leads to the flat 1.2 V discharge curve, the memory effect, hydrogen stored in LaNi5-type alloy, self-discharge (NiO(OH) lies below the O2/OH- rung) and cycle life, plus NiFe and NiH2 as other partners on the potential ladder. Capstone: an AA shoot-out simulator (alkaline primary, NiCd, NiMH x radio, torch, camera flash, with shelf months and repeated runs) plotting terminal voltage vs time and counting cells bought. Hooks for later lessons: 'one H per electron shuttles between two host solids' (rocking-chair preview for lithium-ion), the water rung as the limit for aqueous anodes, load-dependent voltage loss (Real batteries), typical Wh/kg of NiCd and NiMH.
